turns.assistant_text:
Here are the latest AI news highlights for today (July 28, 2026):

---

### 📉 **AI Sell-Off & Market Jitters**
- **AI stocks are tumbling** as investors grow worried about the massive spending required for AI infrastructure. Chip stocks (SK Hynix, Samsung) led the decline in Asia. ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jul/28/ai-sell-off-chip-stocks-sk-hynix-samsung))
- **Nvidia is reportedly in talks** with OpenAI to provide **$250 billion** in financing for a massive data center project in Ohio, raising concerns about "circular financing" in the AI industry. ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/28/business/stocks-ai-chips.html))
- **CXMT**, a Chinese memory chip maker, surged **466%** on its Shanghai IPO debut before slipping 4% today — highlighting China's push for an independent AI supply chain.

### 🏢 **Big Tech AI Moves**
- **Amazon** is phasing out some AI models while doubling down on its **Nova** lineup, focusing resources on its highest priorities. ([MediaPost](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/416869/amazon-phases-out-some-ai-models-advances-others.html))
- **Meta** announced a **$14 billion** deal with BlackRock to build a 1-gigawatt data center in Texas. Meta reports earnings tomorrow.
- **Apple** briefly surpassed **$5 trillion** market cap — the second company ever to do so.

### 🧠 **AI Safety & Research**
- **Wharton researchers** found that basic psychological persuasion tactics can bypass AI safety guardrails — tested on GPT-5 mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, and Gemini 3 Flash. ([Penn Today](https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/wharton-how-basic-persuasion-can-bypass-ai-safeguards))

### 📊 **Workforce & Economy**
- A **Conference Board report** shows most organizations are training workers for today's AI tools, not preparing them for future job shifts. ([PRNewswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/report-most-organizations-are-preparing-workers-for-todays-ai-not-tomorrows-jobs-302836842.html))

---

The dominant theme today is **AI spending anxiety** — investors are questioning whether the massive capital outlays will pay off, especially as Chinese competition heats up.

items.title: Amazon Phases Out Some AI Models, Advances Others
items.summary:
advertisement

advertisement

Amazon’s commitment to building advanced AI models remains as strong as it
has been in the past, the spokesperson said.

The report from Business Insider published today attributed the change to a restructuring of Amazon's AI strategy. "Rather than
investing across a number of text, image, and video models, the company is concentrating engineering talent and scarce computing resources on its highest priorities," Business Insider
wrote. [...] "AI models remain one of the most important things we're working on, and that hasn't changed," an Amazon spokesperson told MediaPost on Tuesday. "We are continuing to invest in
and support the Nova models our customers rely on today, including through Nova Forge, which lets businesses build their own models on Nova as a foundation."

Models in production are typically
supported for extended periods, while continuing to invest in the next generation of frontier model research.

advertisement [...] An Amazon spokesperson acknowledged an early Tuesday morning report by explaining that its AI
portfolios evolve based on customer needs. This is one way that Amazon provides companies, agencies and brands with guidance and migration paths as models advance, and others become
obsolete.

items.summary: The latest A.I.-related market tremor began on Monday, when the shares of China’s leading memory chipmaker, ChangXin Memory Technologies, began trading after a blockbuster initial public offering. items.title: How basic persuasion can bypass AI safeguards - Penn Today
items.summary:
2 min. read

Concerns over “jailbreaking” AI—a way of circumventing the safety guardrails built into large language models—have escalated after the Trump administration ordered Anthropic to pull its latest models, Fable and Mythos, over concerns they could be coaxed into revealing security flaws in software.

View large image [...] In their paper “Persuading Large Language Models to Comply With Objectionable Requests,” the researchers tested models from three leading AI labs: OpenAI’s GPT-5 mini, Anthropic’s Claude Haiku 4.5, and Google’s Gemini 3 Flash, by having 126,000 “conversations” with them. [...] Image: Hanna Barakat  & Archival Images of AI + AIxDESIGN /  / 

Now, timely research from Wharton’s Generative AI Labs (GAIL) suggests the safeguards designed to prevent misuse may be vulnerable to the same psychological tactics that influence people.

items.title: Jerry Gulke: Why AI Can’t Replace Price Risk Management in Corn Markets
items.summary:
(Farm Journal)

I have no doubt Artificial Intelligence, as defined today, will aid in answering a lot of questions regarding production, but I wonder if it will be beneficial in today’s ag-commodity markets as it pertains to price-outlook and price risk management. It currently lacks intuition, experience, proactive analysis, and knowledge of eco-political events, and it doesn’t farm.
